Hi Jordan — attaching short answers below to help your legal team. Happy to jump on a quick call if anything needs finer detail. I’ve also attached the current subprocessors list (subprocessors_list_2027-05.pdf) and links to SOC 2 evidence.

1) Controller / Processor
- Redwood operates as a data processor for customer-provided data; Acme remains the data controller. We process data per documented instructions in the contract and DPA. Standard DPA language we provided reflects this (see Redwood_DPA_v1.pdf).

2) Subprocessors
- Current subprocessors: cloud infra providers (AWS), object storage (S3), monitoring (Datadog), analytics/telemetry (segment-equivalent), and CDN provider. Full list + regions here: https://redwood-internal.kb/subprocessors-list-2027-05.
- We notify customers of material additions and provide a short objection window (30 days) per the DPA; critical infra changes are communicated in advance where possible.

3) Breach notification
- Commitment: Redwood will notify customers without undue delay and no later than 72 hours after confirming a security incident that affects customer data, consistent with common incident response timelines. We’ll provide scope, remediation steps, and follow-up reports.

4) Data residency
- Default: hosted customers may have data stored in the region associated with their account (we currently provide US and EU regions).
- US-only: For production US-only residency we recommend Redwood Dedicated or Private (VPC/on-prem) deployment to ensure contractual residency guarantees. These options are available in procurement and may affect pricing.

5) Retention & deletion
- Default retention: request/response payloads (including PII) are retained for 30 days for debugging and quality monitoring (shorter windows available by contract).
- Access logs: retained by default for 90 days; can be shortened or exported to customer-owned logging depending on plan.
- Accelerated deletion: customers can request deletion of data; we’ll confirm deletion within 30 days of a validated request and provide proof of deletion.

6) Logging controls & PII handling
- Logged fields: timestamps, request IDs, model variant, latency, token counts, worker node IDs, and non-sensitive metadata.
- We do not persist PII fields by default beyond the retention windows above unless needed for debugging - customers can request redaction or pseudonymization.
- Additional controls: streaming can be disabled; configurable prompt scrubbing and deterministic pseudonymization offered for sensitive fields.

7) Certifications & evidence
- SOC 2 Type II report and ISMS summary available under NDA. Link to evidence and how to request it: https://drive.google.com/docs/d/ACME-DPA-QUESTIONS.

If you’d like, we can produce contract language snippets for each answer to drop into the DPA; happy to schedule 30 minutes with legal + engineering.

Best,
Dev Patel
Senior Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
